traditions.label: Trika · Kashmir Shaivism
traditions.blurb: A non-dual Tantric philosophy in which the world is the free, conscious play of Shiva, recognised as one's own self.

courses.title: Kashmir Shaivism: first steps
courses.intro: The non-dual tantra of Kashmir in five talks: how its last great master taught meditation, what tantra really is, why the world is not an illusion, and the Recognition teaching. Two short practices from the tradition's own texts.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: How to meditate in this tradition
unitTitles: How to meditate in this tradition

phases.title: The world is not an illusion
unitTitles: The world is not an illusion

phases.title: A practice from the Vijnana Bhairava
unitTitles: A practice from the Vijnana Bhairava

courses.title: Trika prep week
courses.intro: Seven days of foundation for Abhinavagupta and VBT study: steady breath, the turn of the breath, and recognition. Ten minutes a day. Initiated practices are not here: when the gap is steady, take the next step with a qualified teacher in the tradition.
courses.author: Wiser

courses.title: VBT Foundations
courses.intro: Seven contemplative practices from the Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra, in a progression from the breath to daily life (not the text's own order): the turn of the breath, the gap between objects, inner sound, the body as awareness, the sense spaces, spaciousness, and the end-of-twelve through the day. Each is a quiet sit you can do on your own. The rest of the text (breath retention, mantra, the subtle-body practices) is learned from a qualified teacher: when one of these becomes your door, take it to a teacher in the tradition.
courses.author: Wiser

courses.title: Kashmir Shaivism: a first syllabus
courses.intro: The nondual Śaiva tradition of Kashmir, in six steps: a theory track of short talks from scholars and teachers, and a practice track of simple contemplations from the Vijñāna Bhairava and the Pratyabhijñā.

traditions.label: Theravāda
traditions.blurb: The oldest surviving Buddhist school, rooted in the Pāli discourses and the monastic code; strong today in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

courses.title: Mindfulness of breathing
courses.intro: The Buddha's own meditation, from the first breath to a whole path. Four teachers from three lines, two practices, and the discourse itself.
courses.author: Satsang

courses.title: Loving-kindness, step by step
courses.intro: Metta from the teacher who brought it West, a forest monk who calls it serious practice, Ajahn Brahm at his warmest, a guided sit, and the Tibetan widening into bodhicitta.
courses.author: Satsang

courses.title: Contemplating death
courses.intro: The Buddhist reflection on death as a source of freedom rather than fear: why to practise it, how the suttas teach it, how to rehearse it, and a gentle view of where we go.
courses.author: Satsang

courses.title: How Buddhist rebirth works
courses.intro: What the Buddha taught about death and the next life, why it is not the reincarnation of a soul, and how the Tibetan tradition maps the passage between lives. Five talks, one reflection, two short readings.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: If there is no self, what is reborn?
unitTitles: If there is no self, what is reborn?

courses.title: Past lives: what the texts say, and the ground to stand on
courses.intro: The suttas and the Visuddhimagga describe recollecting former lives as a by-product of a very calm mind, never a goal. Hear how teachers in the forest tradition explain it, build the real foundation (steady breath meditation), and read the sources yourself.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: What the suttas mean by it
unitTitles: What the suttas mean by it

phases.title: Do you have to believe it?
unitTitles: Do you have to believe it?

phases.title: The sources, and the practice as the texts give it
unitTitles: The sources, and the practice as the texts give it

courses.title: Thai Forest: the basics
courses.intro: The forest tradition of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah, as its Western monks teach it today: virtue, the breath, Buddho, walking, and how to bring it into a life.

schools.label: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)

traditions.label: Tibetan Buddhism
traditions.blurb: The Buddhism of the Himalaya, joining monastic study and debate with Vajrayāna practice and guidance for the dying.

courses.title: Visualisations: the Tibetan deity practice primer
courses.intro: Orientation only. Deity yoga is taught in Tibetan Buddhism after an empowerment and with a teacher; this primer explains what it is and why it is practised, through talks by teachers of the tradition. It does not teach the visualisations themselves.

traditions.label: Zen
traditions.blurb: Chan and Zen: awakening through sitting, direct pointing and the teacher–student encounter, more than through scripture.

courses.title: Zen: just sitting
courses.intro: Why Zen sits, what just sitting is, and the two great roads: silent illumination and the koan. Teachers from Soto, Rinzai-style koan practice and Chan.
courses.author: Satsang

traditions.label: Chan
traditions.blurb: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

traditions.label: Mahāyāna
traditions.blurb: The "great vehicle": the bodhisattva ideal of awakening for the sake of all beings, and the teaching of emptiness.

traditions.label: Occult · Western esotericism
traditions.blurb: Western paths of hidden knowledge: Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

schools.label: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn

courses.title: Middle Pillar week
courses.intro: One outline, seven sittings. Each day adds one centre to the pillar, then rests in the circulation. Ten minutes a day. This is orientation only: the full form is learnt in the order or from a qualified teacher.
courses.author: Wiser

courses.title: Hermeticism and the Middle Pillar: an orientation
courses.intro: Where Western esotericism comes from: the Hermetic writings, the Golden Dawn, and its best-known exercise shown in outline. A scholar's history first, then one contemplative reading of the Corpus Hermeticum.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: Ascent and rebirth in the Hermetica
unitTitles: Ascent and rebirth in the Hermetica

traditions.label: Vedānta
traditions.blurb: Philosophy built on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Brahma Sūtras, asking how the self relates to Brahman.

courses.title: Self-enquiry: who am I?
courses.intro: Ramana Maharshi's question, taught by three living teachers: what the enquiry is, how to do it, and what it is not. One practice to take into the day.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: Who am I if not the knower?
unitTitles: Who am I if not the knower?

traditions.label: Śaivism
traditions.blurb: Umbrella for Śiva-centred traditions: the ascetic Atimārga and the initiatory Mantramārga.

traditions.label: Śāktism
traditions.blurb: Goddess-centred traditions; parent of Kaula, Śrī Vidyā and Kālī lines.

traditions.label: Sufism
traditions.blurb: The inner, mystical path of Islam: remembrance of God (dhikr), the master and the order, the poetry of love.

courses.title: Sufi remembrance (dhikr)
courses.intro: The Sufi path of love and remembrance: what dhikr is, how breath and the divine name meet, the imaginal world of the Sufis, and the women of the tradition.
courses.author: Satsang

traditions.label: Christian traditions
traditions.blurb: The traditions that follow Jesus of Nazareth, from the Gospels and the early Church to the mystics.

courses.title: Christian contemplative prayer
courses.intro: The quiet heart of Christianity: the hesychasts and the Cloud of Unknowing, the Jesus Prayer, lectio divina and meditation with a prayer word.
courses.author: Satsang

traditions.label: Jewish mysticism
traditions.blurb: Merkavah, Kabbalah, the Zohar and Hasidism: the contemplative and mystical currents of Judaism.

traditions.label: Platonic tradition
traditions.blurb: Philosophy as the care of the soul, turning from the world of change toward the eternal Forms and the Good.

courses.title: Plotinus and the ascent to the One
courses.intro: The Western contemplative root: Plotinus' map of the One, Intellect and Soul, why the soul descends, how it turns back, and what "alone with the Alone" means. Two practices from the Platonic tradition.
courses.author: Satsang

traditions.label: Vajrayāna
traditions.blurb: Tantric Buddhism: deity practice, mantra and the teacher's transmission as a swift path to awakening.

courses.title: Metta in four traditions
courses.intro: Goodwill, loving-kindness, compassion: four ways of growing a kind heart, one sit at a time.

courses.title: Rebirth across traditions
courses.intro: Does anything carry on after death? One talk from each tradition that answers, then the classic texts to read for free.

courses.title: Seven days with death
courses.intro: One short talk and one practice a day for a week. The traditions agree on little, but they agree that remembering death changes how we live. Go gently; skip a day whenever you need to.
courses.author: Satsang

phases.title: The moment of death and after
unitTitles: The moment of death and after
